key_insight: LLM agents can turn household preferences into executable home-energy schedules and achieve near-MILP optimality, especially when using native function calling.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical path for deploying natural-language interfaces in home energy management to reduce electricity costs while respecting appliance, tariff, and safety constraints.
method: ReAct tool-calling agent with live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV generation estimates, and household usage data
Retrieval-augmented knowledge base plus MILP ground-truth scheduling for flexible loads
Benchmark across commercial LLMs under tariff, constraint-conflict, solar co-optimization, and week-long deployment scenarios
evidence_signal: Across three models, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and 96.7-98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week, with near-MILP performance.
watch_item: Text-parsed action interfaces were much less reliable than native function calling, so real deployments need robust tool integration and constraint handling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
